shared_elements: low-relief carving on a standing/upright stone surface
curved incised bands suggesting a bent arm or limb
protruding rounded/cylindrical boss or knob-like element set on the surface
linear incised outlines with plain infill
justification: Both surfaces show shallow incised outline carving on an upright monolithic face in which curved parallel bands read as a bent arm, with a rounded projecting boss (a disc on the torso in A, a cylindrical knob apparently held or set at the arm's end in B), a fairly specific combination of flat linear relief plus a raised circular element. The biggest difference is that A presents a complete anthropomorphic figure with head, headgear, folded arms and banded belt in a legible whole-body scheme, while B shows only an isolated fragment of limb-and-knob with no readable figure, body plan or accompanying motifs to confirm the same scheme.
